Per the project's stored release convention, a release is cut by pushing a tag. CI does the rest.

1. Make sure what you want to ship is on `main`.
2. Tag it as `vYYYY.MM.N`. `N` is the release counter within that month. For example, `v2026.09.2` was the second release in September 2026. Today is 2026-10-01, so the first October release would be `v2026.10.1`.
   ```
   git tag v2026.10.1
   git push origin v2026.10.1
   ```
3. CI then builds the artifacts, runs the full test suite and publishes the release. Don't publish packages by hand.

I couldn't confirm this from the repo itself. There's no `.github/workflows` directory, and I didn't check the `Makefile` or `scripts/`. The process comes from a single memory entry, so check the CI config wherever it lives before relying on it. I also don't know whether `N` restarts at 1 each month. The example suggests it does, so check the existing tags with `git tag` before choosing one.

I haven't created or pushed any tag.
